complaint_hint: What is the problem observed in the vehicle?
triage_q1: Triage Check 1 of 3 — Power Supply: With ignition ON and the ABS 3rd braking relay active, is +24V present at the Green wire of the Customer Mating Connector?
triage_q2: Triage Check 2 of 3 — Relay Energization: With brake pressed and speed > 5 km/h, does the Relay Box click / energize?
triage_q3: Triage Check 3 of 3 — Relay Output: Is +24V present at the top fused output terminal of the Relay Box?
int_q1: Intermittent Check 1 of 5 — Connector Seating: Are ALL connector locking clips fully clicked and secure?
int_q2: Intermittent Check 2 of 5 — Pin Corrosion: Are all connector pins free from green oxidation or corrosion?
int_q3: Intermittent Check 3 of 5 — Harness Routing: Is the Signal Wiring Harness free from chafing, pinching, or heat damage?
int_q4: Intermittent Check 4 of 5 — Ground Resistance: Is ground resistance less than 0.5 Ω?
int_q5: Intermittent Check 5 of 5 — Final Retest: After all corrections, is the intermittent fault resolved?
green: With Vehicle ignition ON, is Green (+24V supply) present at the customer mating connector?
green_fuse: Is 10A fuse OK in the vehicle fuse box?
green_vehicle_conn: Check vehicle connection/wiring from fuse/relay to mating connector. After fixing, re-check Green (+24V). Is +24V present now?
black: Is Black (Ground) OK (good continuity / low drop)?
yellow: Is Yellow/White (Vehicle Speed digital signal) present? (Check frequency: should be > 15 Hz while wheels rotate)
sb_green: Is +24V present on the Green wire at the ECU Speed Box connector?
sb_green_continuity: Check continuity between Customer Mating Connector and ECU Speed Box (Green wire). Is it OK?
sb_black: Is Ground (Black) OK at ECU Speed Box (low drop / good continuity to chassis)?
sb_black_continuity: Check continuity between Customer Mating Connector and ECU Speed Box (Black wire). Is it OK?
sb_bypass_check: Is Yellow/White (vehicle speed) reaching the Speed Booster bypass and continuing as Yellow/White to the ECU Speed Box?
sb_yellow_path: Check continuity between Customer Mating Connector (Yellow/White) and Speed Box Booster connector (Yellow/White). Is it OK?
sb_grey_pulses: With wheels rotating (>5 km/h), are speed pulses present on the Yellow/White wire at ECU Speed Box input? (Check frequency: should be > 15 Hz)
sb_violet_output: With Green=24V, Black=GND and Yellow/White pulses present, when vehicle speed > 5 km/h does ECU Speed Box output (Violet) go to 24V?
sw_violet_input: With vehicle speed > 5 km/h and ECU Speed Box working, is +24V present at the Violet wire (Switch Input)?
sw_violet_continuity: Check continuity between ECU Speed Box connector and Retarder Switch connector. Is it OK?
sw_pink_output: Turn switch ON. With speed > 5 km/h (Violet=24V), does the Pink wire (Switch Output) show 24V (ON) and 0V (OFF)?
aps_pin1_input: With Retarder Switch ON and vehicle speed > 5 km/h, is 24V present at the Pink wire of the Air Pressure Switch Connector?
aps_pin1_continuity: Check continuity between Retarder Switch and Air Pressure Switch (Signal Wiring Harness). Is it OK?
aps_pin1_recheck: After confirming continuity, check the Pink wire again for 24V. Is it present now?
aps_internal_supply:
With 24V confirmed at Pink, is supply distributed internally to all 4 stage inputs in air pressure switch?

• Slide back rubber boot carefully
• Identify common supply wire (C5 – harness tag reference)
• Ensure safe probing method
aps_output_check:
Press brake to increase air pressure. Does at least ONE pin (out of 1, 2, 3, or 4) show 24V output from the switches?

• Identify output supply wire (C1, C2, C3 or C4 – harness tag reference)
aps_hose_check: Press brake and check air hose: Is air pressure actually reaching the manifold through the hose?
rb_precheck_pins: Inspect terminals: Is the 8-pin connector free from corrosion or bent pins?
rb_precheck_locked: Is the connector locking clip fully engaged and locked?
rb_cutoff_pos: Is the Cut-off switch ON and does the Relay Box power up?
rb_cutoff_output: Measure Cut-off switch OUTPUT terminal. Is +24V present (Switch ON)?
rb_cutoff_input: Measure Cut-off switch INPUT terminal (from battery). Is +24V present?
rb_battery_check: Check directly at Battery terminals. Is +24V present?
rb_verify_ground: Is the relay box negative cable connected to chassis ground?
rb_ground_contact: Is there bare metal-to-metal contact at the ground point (no paint/rust)?
rb_negative_cable_condition: Is the negative cable healthy (not broken, cut, or corroded)?
rb_aps_signal_check: With brake pressed, is 24V signal reaching the relay from the Air Pressure Switch?
rb_energization: Does the relay energize (click) when positive, ground, and signal are present?
rb_fuse_check: Are the relay fuses (F1 / F2 / F3 / F4) healthy?
rb_output_check: Is +24V present at the TOP fused output terminal of the relay?
rb_final_confirmation: Confirm all systems: Supply, Grounds, Signals, Fuses, and Energization OK?
ret_mb_check: Check MB Connector Wiring Harness: Is it free from physical damage or corrosion?
ret_power_check: Check Power Wiring Harness: Is it free from cuts, damage, or corrosion?
ret_coil_ground_check: Check Ground: Is there NO continuity between retarder earth terminal and chassis (Isolation OK)?

wf-conn_note:
💡 BSVI Vehicle Connector Color Code:
Black = Negative  |  Yellow/White = Speed Signal  |  Green = Positive*  |  Green/White = MB Indicator.
*Positive: 24V positive from the 3rd braking (ABS 3rd relay) positive.
wf-speed_note:
💡 ECU Speed Box Logic: The ECU Speed Box validates vehicle speed and enables the retarder only when speed exceeds 5 km/h.
It prevents retarder activation at standstill or very low speed.
wf-switch_note: 💡 Switch Logic: The dashboard retarder switch acts as an enable gate. When turned ON, it passes the 24V output from the ECU Speed Box to the Air Pressure Switch.
wf-aps_note:
💡 Safety Cut-off: The Air Pressure Switch converts brake air pressure into electrical signals to activate the retarder in stages.
Without air pressure input, the retarder will not function.
wf-relay_note: 💡 Power Stage: The Relay Box switches high-current battery power to the retarder coils based on low-current stage signals from the Air Pressure Switch.
wf-retarder_note: 💡 Retarder Logic: A retarder provides auxiliary braking to reduce vehicle speed without using the service (friction) brakes.

odo_recommendation_text:
🔹 Replace Silent Block Assembly (Part No: 96943110) every 2,00,000 km (preventive replacement interval) due to rubber ageing, loss of damping efficiency, and to avoid misalignment & bracket stress.
🔹 Even if no cracks are visible, the rubber hardens and loses elasticity over time.
🔹 Ensures proper vibration isolation, safety, and protects the chassis bracket and mounting hardware.

No pulses at Grey wire. Need to isolate: No pulses at Yellow/White wire. Need to isolate if the issue is with the signal path (bypass) or the vehicle speed source itself.
Bypass not fitted/loose or wiring open. Fit/reseat bypass and repair Yellow/White continuity. Resolve it before continuing.

No +24V at mating connector. Check 10A f: No +24V at mating connector. Check 10A fuse in the vehicle fuse box and ABS 3rd relay. Replace the faulty component and retest from this step.
Relay not energizing. Suspect signal pat: Relay not energizing. Suspect signal path fault — verify: ① Retarder Switch is ON, ② Air Pressure Switch has brake air pressure, ③ ECU Speed Box Violet output = 24V at speed > 5 km/h. Switch to NOT WORKING mode for full guided diagnosis.
Power supply chain is healthy. Fault is: Power supply chain is healthy. Fault is in the retarder unit side — inspect MB Connector Harness and Power Wiring Harness for cuts, corrosion, or damage.
Relay Box not switching output. Replace: Relay Box not switching output. Replace with Kit Relay Box Part No: 96503095.
Reseat all loose connectors firmly until: Reseat all loose connectors firmly until they click. Vibration is the #1 cause of intermittent retarder faults — a connector that looks seated may not be fully locked.
Corroded pins cause high-resistance inte: Corroded pins cause high-resistance intermittent contact. Clean with electrical contact cleaner and a pin cleaning brush. If oxidation is severe or pins are damaged, replace the affected harness.
Damaged harness insulation causes interm: Damaged harness insulation causes intermittent open or short circuit under vibration or heat. Reroute harness away from sharp edges and heat sources. Protect with split conduit. Replace Signal Wiring Harness if wire insulation is cut or melted.
High ground resistance (> 0.5 Ω) causes: High ground resistance (> 0.5 Ω) causes voltage-sensitive intermittent faults under load. Scrape chassis ground point to bare metal, clean and retighten firmly.
Intermittent fault persists after connec: Intermittent fault persists after connector and ground checks. A deeper electrical fault is present — switch to NOT WORKING mode and follow the full step-by-step guided diagnosis for complete fault isolation.

tml_stop_abs_action:
Root Cause: ABS System Malfunction detected by Vehicle ECU.
Corrective Action: Inspect and rectify the ABS system using OEM Diagnostic Tool.
tml_stop_hsa_action:
Root Cause: Hill Start Assist (HSA) Malfunction detected by Vehicle ECU.
Corrective Action: Inspect and rectify the HSA system using OEM Diagnostic Tool.
tml_stop_slip_action:
Root Cause: Wheel Slip / Traction Control Fault detected by Vehicle ECU.
Corrective Action: Inspect and rectify the traction/slip control system.
tml_ecs_3_1_q: Is 24V available at the battery supply terminal of the ECS Box Assembly?
tml_end_ecs_3_1_action:
Root Cause: Battery supply fault between Battery and ECS Box Assembly.
Corrective Action: Inspect battery terminals, cable condition, and connections. Rectify open/loose circuits and verify 24V supply.
tml_end_ecs_3_2_action:
Root Cause: 200A Fuse Open / Failed.
Corrective Action: Replace 200A Fuse.
tml_ecs_3_3_q: With Vehicle Ignition ON, is 24V available at the output terminal of the Battery Cut-Off Relay Unit feeding the ECS Box Assembly?
tml_end_ecs_3_3_action:
Root Cause: Battery Cut-Off Relay Unit Internal Failure.
Corrective Action: Replace Battery Cut-Off Relay Unit.
tml_ecs_3_4_q: Is negative cable properly connected and continuity available?
tml_end_ecs_3_4_action:
Root Cause: High resistance / Ground path fault (Loose connection, corrosion, or damaged cable).
Corrective Action: Tighten terminals, clean ground points, and repair negative cable.
tml_ecs_3_5_q: Is ECS Power Harness properly connected between ECS Box Assembly and vehicle system?
tml_end_ecs_3_5_action:
Root Cause: ECS Power Harness damaged or loosely connected.
Corrective Action: Repair harness, replace damaged pins/connectors, and rectify loose connections.
tml_veh_pin1_q: After switching ignition OFF and disconnecting the 8-pin connector, measure the Pin 1 (Yellow) CAN-H terminal. With ignition ON for the test, is the voltage above 2.5V?
tml_end_pin1_action: Inspect CAN Harness, Check Connector Pins, Repair Wiring and Retest.
tml_veh_pin2_q: After switching ignition OFF and disconnecting the 8-pin connector, measure the Pin 2 (Green) CAN-L terminal. With ignition ON for the test, is the voltage below 2.5V?
tml_end_pin2_action: Inspect CAN Harness, Check Connector Pins, Repair Wiring and Retest.
tml_veh_pin3_q:
⚠️ Please Turn ON the Vehicle Ignition.

Pin 3 (Red) - Ignition Input: Is voltage 24V?
tml_end_pin3_action: Verify Ignition ON, Check Vehicle Fuse, Check Red Wire Continuity, Repair and Retest.
tml_veh_pin4_q: After switching ignition OFF and disconnecting the 8-pin connector, measure the Pin 4 (Violet) terminal. With the retarder switch ON for the test, is the input approximately 24V?
tml_end_pin4_sw_ok_action: Switch Healthy. Check Violet Wire, Connector, Dashboard Wiring.
tml_veh_pin5_q: With ignition OFF and the 8-pin connector disconnected, check continuity between Pin 5 (Black) and vehicle negative. Is the ground path continuous?
tml_end_pin5_action: Check Negative Supply Continuity, Inspect Ground Connection/Chassis Point, Repair and Retest.
tml_veh_pin8_q: With ignition OFF and the 8-pin connector disconnected, check continuity between Pin 8 (Black) and vehicle negative. Is the ground path continuous?
tml_end_pin8_action: Check Negative Supply Continuity, Inspect Ground Wire, Check Chassis Ground Connection, Repair and Retest.

tml_not_engaging_q: Is air pressure reaching the retarder when activated?
tml_trial_2_q: Is the retarder indication displayed in the instrument cluster?
tml_trial_3_sub: Condition: Retarder switched OFF or brake demand removed.

tml_ps1_q: Hose Condition — Is the hose connected properly, without kinks or leaks?
tml_end_ps1_action: Reconnect or Replace Hose if damaged. Retest Vehicle.
tml_ps2_q: Pressure Switch Assembly Connection — Is the connector locked properly, with intact wiring and no corrosion?
tml_ps3_q: Pressure Block Inspection — Are there no cracks, air leaks, or blockages?
tml_end_ps3_action: Replace Pressure Block (BIPL: 96633887 / TML: 516554509902). Retest Vehicle.
tml_ps4_sub: Vehicle Condition: Retarder OFF, Brake Pedal Released, Speed > 5 km/h.
tml_ps4_q: Pressure Release Verification — After the retarder is OFF and the brake pedal is released, has the air pressure been released at the Pressure Switch?
tml_end_ps4_action: Pressure trapped. Repair or replace faulty pneumatic components (Pressure block restriction / Hose restriction) and retest.
tml_ps5_sub: Condition: No pressure applied to the Pressure Switch.
tml_ps5_q: Pressure Switch Output Test — Is the Pressure Switch output still ON (5V)?
tml_sol1_q: Solenoid Valve Resistance — Is the resistance within specification (approximately 12–16 ohms)?
tml_sol2_q: Solenoid Valve Operation — Does it click when 24V is applied?
tml_end_sol2_action: Replace Solenoid Valve due to mechanical failure. Retest Vehicle.
tml_end_sol_ok_action: Solenoid & pneumatics operate normally. Problem is likely internal to the retarder (mechanical failure/seals). Inspect Retarder Mechanicals.

tml_location_phase_1: Instrument cluster in front of the driver. Check the retarder and warning indicators with ignition ON.
tml_location_phase_2: Locate the Blink Code switch in the driver switch panel. Use it to read the retarder blink code.
tml_location_phase_3: Locate the ECS box assembly on the vehicle chassis. Inspect the box, fuse, relay, and nearby wiring as directed by the step.
tml_location_phase_4: Locate the ECS 8-pin connector in the harness at the ECS assembly. Check the connector lock and terminals as directed by the step.
tml_location_phase_5: Locate the air-pressure switch assembly below the driver brake pedal. Follow workshop safety procedures before inspection.
tml_location_phase_6: Retarder assembly mounted on the driveline. Follow workshop safety procedures before inspection.
tml_location_pressure_switch_1: Locate the air-pressure switch and manifold assembly. Inspect the air inlet hose, fittings, pressure block, and switch connections for leaks, kinks, or damage.
tml_location_pressure_switch_2: Inspect the pressure-switch connector and wiring at the air-pressure switch/manifold assembly. Confirm the connector lock, terminals, and harness condition.
tml_location_pressure_switch_3: Inspect the pressure block/manifold body and all pneumatic joints for cracks, blockage, or air leakage.
tml_location_pressure_switch_4: Check the pressure-switch release path at the air-pressure switch and manifold after the retarder is turned OFF and the brake pedal is released.
tml_location_pressure_switch_5: Inspect the pressure-switch electrical output connector and terminals. Measure the output only with the approved workshop procedure.
tml_location_solenoid_valve_1: Locate the solenoid valve/manifold assembly. With power isolated, measure the solenoid coil resistance using the approved workshop procedure.
tml_location_solenoid_valve_2: Locate the solenoid valve/manifold assembly and listen or feel for operation only under the approved 24V test procedure.
